paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend: God doesn't just save you, He builds with you. Peter says you are "like living stones," being built into a spiritual house (1 Peter 2:5). That's why he starts with clean-up and cravings: get rid of the junk, and go after pure spiritual milk so you can "grow up in your salvation" (1 Peter 2:1-2). You are not a pile of rocks lying in the yard, you are part of a BUILDING.

And look at who the building rests on. The stone men rejected is "chosen and precious in God's sight" (1 Peter 2:4), and the one who believes in Him "will never be put to shame" (1 Peter 2:6). I know a little about being tossed aside, and let me tell you, how people see you does not get the last word. God's view of Jesus is the one that stands, and when you come to Him, you stand on it too. Some stumble over that stone because they disobey the word, but for you who believe, He is precious (1 Peter 2:7-8).

So what are you now? "A chosen people, a royal priesthood, a holy nation, a people for God's own possession" (1 Peter 2:9). Once you were not a people, but now you are the people of God, and once you had not received mercy, but now you have (1 Peter 2:10). That is not a title to tuck in a drawer, friend. You were called out of darkness into His marvelous light, and the job is to proclaim the virtues of the One who called you (1 Peter 2:9).
